BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Crawfish Solar Holdings 2, LLC is the parent of the 300 MW Oxbow solar farm in Louisiana and the 95 MW Happy solar farm in Arkansas.

JERA Nex and Schroders Greencoat each own 50% following the July 30, 2025 sell-down to SG US Aggregator LLC. Lightsource bp sold the portfolio to JERA in 2024 and continues to provide asset-management and O&M services without a current common-equity interest.

STORY TIMELINE
Jul 30, 2025
Investment

Schroders Greencoat acquired 50% through SG US Aggregator LLC, creating a 50:50 partnership with JERA Nex.

Aug 2, 2024
Investment

JERA Nex completed its acquisition of 100% of the Oxbow and Happy portfolio from Lightsource bp.

May 2024
Expansion

Oxbow Solar began commercial operation in Louisiana.

2023
Expansion

Happy Solar began commercial operation in Arkansas; primary sources differ between September and October.

api.description: Unison Energy, LLC develops, finances, builds, owns, operates and maintains behind-the-meter microgrids and distributed-energy systems for commercial and industrial customers across North America. Its primary model uses long-term energy-service agreements and project SPVs, while the company also supports customer-owned EPC, operations-and-maintenance and hybrid structures; not every system is therefore owned by Unison. The platform serves healthcare, data-center, industrial, hospitality, logistics and other resilience-sensitive facilities using combined heat and power, controls, solar, batteries and thermal systems. At Tiger's June 2024 entry, public materials described approximately 30 operating or signed-ESA projects and about 26 MW installed; a current aggregate scale is not publicly disclosed. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III acquired control through Fund III AIV U LP on June 17, 2024 from American Infrastructure Funds/AIM Universal and Hunt Companies. Exact percentages and consideration were not disclosed, and no later sale or signed ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Unison Energy, LLC develops, finances, builds, owns, operates and maintains behind-the-meter microgrids and distributed-energy systems for commercial and industrial customers across North America. Its primary model uses long-term energy-service agreements and project SPVs, while the company also supports customer-owned EPC, operations-and-maintenance and hybrid structures; not every system is therefore owned by Unison. The platform serves healthcare, data-center, industrial, hospitality, logistics and other resilience-sensitive facilities using combined heat and power, controls, solar, batteries and thermal systems. At Tiger's June 2024 entry, public materials described approximately 30 operating or signed-ESA projects and about 26 MW installed; a current aggregate scale is not publicly disclosed. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III acquired control through Fund III AIV U LP on June 17, 2024 from American Infrastructure Funds/AIM Universal and Hunt Companies. Exact percentages and consideration were not disclosed, and no later sale or signed ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

STORY TIMELINE
Jun 17, 2024
Investment

Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III closed its controlling acquisition and growth investment in Unison Energy from AIF/AIM Universal and Hunt Companies.

2013

Andy Cooper and Tim Lukes founded Unison Energy to develop and operate distributed-energy and microgrid systems.
